# key <TAB> site VA (game VA of the signature's first byte = the arm's find_pattern base) <TAB> signature (IDA format, one ? per wildcard byte) <TAB> signature length in bytes.
# BuildingDynamicShadows has a second anchor (0x8F7420, 50 68 04 01 00 00 6A 02); see the report.
# (the E9 at the match; the shim replays the twelve bytes and resumes at match+12)
# and the four anchors of its site writes. At the first anchor the arm writes `EB`
# at +6, `E9` at +95 (to match+476) and `EB` at +379, retargets the `movss` operand
# at +211 at the module's offset float, and its handler tail rewrites the two push
# immediates and the `je` below with their own recovered bytes.
# CarDynamicShadowFix's old-build pieces are absent from the 1.0.8.0 IDB, so there is
# no site VA to record for them: the pattern-B body anchor
# rewrite at +3, and the @noE six-byte NOP fill at +62 (its own recovered gate, build
# ids 1000 and 1040). CarPartsShadowFix's second standalone site
# (`83 FA 04 75 0C`, +3) is the same kind of old-build variant.
# HighFPSBikePhysicsFix: the detour replaces the site's first five bytes; the
# resume the arm publishes is the site's own `call` at match+9.

# in row order: 0x8FEC12/0x8FEC46 (row 1, both hits), 0xB1D8CB/0xB20EB7 (row 2, both
# The two episode-flag operands are 0x495040 and 0xA84ABE here, 0x421500 and 0xBD91AE
# on 1.0.7.0 (both patterns carry the build's own operand bytes).
# IncreaseVehicleModelLimit: the loop-tail anchor; the arm writes through the dword
# at match+77 (the `mov ecx, 0xF3E8E8` operand), which is the model-limit object.
# PlayerAsPedComponentsFix: the arm's site (the 7-byte `movzx edx,[eax+219h]` inside
# SET_CHAR_COMPONENT_VARIATION, installed at +5) and the model-index lookup the
# shared library resolves with the same pattern the original scans for.
# BadPlayerModelCrashFix: the game's model-resolution entry, three bytes into the
# function (so EBP is live), which the arm replaces with a jump to the body at
# 0x10037BA0; the resume it publishes is the anchor's +10. The three rows below are
# what the original's own loader preamble scans for on every run and this key's
# bodies read: the ped-model object array (dword_1015AD78, the absolute operand four
# bytes before its anchor), the model-class lookup the fallback calls
# (dword_10159C74 = anchor - 42) and the build probe whose *absence* installs the
# ten fallback hash salts (the three this key reads included).
# RemoveStaticCutsceneCarShadows is the cutscene copy of the row above: the store's
# source register differs (44 here, 4C in game) and the `jbe`/`jmp` operand is the
# same, so the arm writes `EB` at +6 exactly as it does there.
# BorderlessWindowed: one `FF 15` call is one site, and the 1.0.8.0 image has two -
# the Unicode window proc's and the ANSI one's. One scan with a two-hit count feeds
# NoImpostorHeightCutoff: one pattern, two sites, both NOPped (the original's block
# writes hits[0] and hits[1]). On 1.0.0.0 the pattern matches once and the original
# writes through an uninitialised vector entry; that fault is reproduced.
# NoLODLightHeightCutoff: a single site; the original's finder returns one match and
# skips cleanly when it is missing.
# CutsceneFixes, chain B: the two places the game's camera function (0xC9A640) is
# called. Each row's match starts five bytes after the `E8` the arm replaces, so
# the call is at match-5 and its destination is `match + [match-4]`; that is what
# the publish reads before the call is overwritten (dword_1015BDE4, and +0x4F into
# dword_1015BDF0). Both sites call the same function, so the second publishes
# nothing. Chain A's `je` in that function becomes `EB`; its first pattern is the
# row below, and the older builds' fallback (`74 0B 83 7C 24 2C 03`, 7 bytes) is
# absent from the 1.0.8.0 image, so it has no site VA to record.
# Patch6and7RemoveModChecks: the only two gated builds are 1.0.6.0 and 1.0.7.0, so these
# rows are the site VAs in THOSE images (base 0x400000); the only IDB available is 1.0.8.0.
# Each signature was confirmed to have exactly one hit on its build.
# loading module (source/loading.ixx): each pattern confirmed with find_bytes against the
# 1.0.8.0 IDB, exactly one hit at the recorded VA except StartupTimeFix (three sites).
# LocalSettingsPath's fallback epilogue, VSyncFix's two anchors, BenchmarkFix's anchor and
# SkipMenu's two alternates are recovered from their handlers but absent from this image;
# their keys are build-gated to builds without an IDB here (no site VA to record).
# DrivebyFOVFix: the site's `movss xmm0,[esi+60h]`; the install is the five-byte jump
# that replaces it and the resume is the `subss xmm1, xmm2` at the anchor's +5.
# The native-script call layer's resolver scan (source/native.ixx, not a catalogue
# key): the original's own loader preamble scans for this and takes the target of the
# call at +5 (match + 10 + the dword at +6), which is 0x626AF0 on 1.0.8.0.
# misc module (source/misc.ixx), confirmed with a byte scan of game_refs/GTAIV.exe
# (1.0.8.0, base 0x400000): exactly one hit at each recorded VA. SpeedupBugFix's
# anchor is the function prologue the arm jumps 21 bytes before; the body's own
# one-time clock scan is recorded separately. Patch4RemoveModChecks and
# RemoveGFWLUpdatePopup share one site (the same shared original stub).
# The shared IDE hook: CopSirensFlag and PopupHeadlightsFlag both install the
# same body at the anchor's -10 (the parser's seven-byte compare).
# Absent on 1.0.8.0 (no site VA to record): PopupHeadlightsFlag's EDX twin
# (0F BF 56 2E 3B 15 ? ? ? ? 75 ? A1) and Patch4RemoveModChecks' Patch4 scan
# (33 C4 89 84 24 A8 01 00 00 53 8B 5D 08 56 57), which the helper runs once at
# run time and which matches nothing on this image.
# (1.0.8.0, base 0x400000): one hit at each recorded VA.
# NewMemorySystem: the anchor is the allocator init's `cmp eax, 0x59999980`; the arm
# retargets the `call` 34 bytes before it and jumps at -29, retargeting the call to
# body 0x10038670 and skipping to -16. The second row is the allocator singleton's
# address (the arm publishes it as dword_10159CD8): `mov esi, 0x19CF9F0`.
# NewFilesCompatibility: the two file-type update calls (the arm retargets each E8)
# and the registrar's `call <entry>`; the arm jumps at +28, which is the registrar's

column1: # The steer/engine/plane consumer sub_10004C70 and its site set (source/vehicles.ixx).
# share one handler in the original -- sub_10005210 first, then the shared IDE parser
# hook sub_10004110 -- so they share every row here.
# The four preamble scans that resolve the consumer's game entries, in the order the
# original resolves them (0x10052EE6..0x10052F50); none is an arm site.
# The vtable-call site the 1.0.6.0-and-later builds carry; the arm jumps its +2 and
# publishes match+16 as the resume and the call operand at match+423/+427 as the
# part-drive function. The older builds' variant
# (7C E0 8B 06 8B 90 28 01 00 00 8B CE FF D2, jump at +2, resume +16, operand
# +140/+144) is absent from the 1.0.8.0 image, so it has no site VA to record.
# The shared IDE parser hook: the arm jumps the anchor's -10 and publishes -1 as its
# resume. The same row is CopSirensFlag's and PopupHeadlightsFlag's (0x646546).
# GarageModelFix: the colour site (jump at match, resume match+6) and the model
# reassignment site (jump at match, resume match+5).
# NoLiveryLimit: the collector site (jump at match+2, resume match+90, lookup operand
# at match-6/-2) and the livery anchor (three jumps at match, -199 and -237, resume
# (8D AF 3C 01 00 00 8D 54 24 20, jump at match, resume match+84, operand at
# match-8/-4) is absent from the 1.0.8.0 image.
# OutOfCommissionFix (source/ooc.ixx): the two anchors the original handler scans
# for itself. The first starts on the last byte of the `mov eax, <magic>` that
# precedes the script resource's compare, so the E9 the arm writes at match+7
# lands on the compare (and the body's resume, match+0x11, on the `movq` store two
# instructions later). The second is the device lookup the wrapper replaces: the
# E8 at the match, whose target the wrapper replays after mounting, and the call
# at match-0x33, which is the game's device register -- the function that takes
# the "memory:$<ptr>,<bytes>,0:" string. Both anchors are unique on 1.0.8.0. The
# branch anchor is absent from 1.0.0.0 and the wrapper anchor from 1.0.0.0,
# 1.0.4.0 and 1.0.0.4; a miss is the original's own clean skip, so those builds
# install only the half their image carries.
